data.description:
## Incident Overview

Concrete failure on d076 epic: orchestrator pushed commit 3f8f62d337 (7 valid Copilot finding fixes + 1 duplicate-CI-trigger fix) to branch story/d076-d35e-55db-4843/2abb-11b6-37ca-49dc at 22:26 UTC. PR #140 had auto-merged the same branch at 22:23 UTC. The push succeeded — git/origin are happy — but the commit is stranded: PR #140 is MERGED, so the new commit has no path to main.

This is the SECOND auto-merge timing miss in the d076 epic. The first was implicit (per-branch review approving an older commit than expected). This one is explicit: commits authored AFTER the merge cannot reach main via the merged PR.

## Failure Mode

1. Orchestrator (or human) has an open PR with auto-merge enabled.
2. CI completes; auto-merge fires; PR merges.
3. Orchestrator pushes additional commits to the same branch (typical pattern when addressing review findings or adding follow-up fixes).
4. Push succeeds. No error. No warning.
5. Commits sit on the remote branch indefinitely; never reach main.
6. Discovered only when someone notices the diff isn't in main, OR when a downstream CI/review confusion surfaces.

## Proposed Hardening (three tiers)

### Tier A — git pre-push hook (strongest)

Add a check to `plugins/dso/hooks/pre-push-*.sh` (or as a new dedicated hook):

```bash
BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
PR_STATE=$(gh pr view "$BRANCH" --json state --jq .state 2>/dev/null || echo "")
case "$PR_STATE" in
    MERGED)
        echo "ERROR: PR for $BRANCH is MERGED. New commits will not flow into main." >&2
        echo "       Open a follow-up PR from origin/main instead. Override: DSO_ALLOW_PUSH_TO_MERGED_PR=1" >&2
        [[ "\${DSO_ALLOW_PUSH_TO_MERGED_PR:-}" == "1" ]] || exit 1 ;;
    CLOSED)
        echo "WARN: PR for $BRANCH is CLOSED. Push may not reach main." >&2 ;;
esac
```

Fail-open when:
- gh is not authenticated (CI runners w/o gh setup)
- No PR exists for the branch (genuine pre-PR push)
- The branch is not push-tracked (local-only branch)

### Tier B — orchestrator wrappers

`merge-to-main.sh` and sprint Phase F should pre-check the PR state for the branch they're about to push to and refuse with a similar message if MERGED. Catches orchestrator-driven pushes specifically (the d076 case).

### Tier C — CLAUDE.md rule

Add to "Never do these" or "Always do these": "Before pushing additional commits to a branch with an open PR, check that the PR is still OPEN (`gh pr view <branch> --json state`). If MERGED, open a follow-up PR instead."

## Test Coverage

- Pre-push hook fires on a branch whose PR is MERGED → exit non-zero
- Pre-push hook allows push when PR is OPEN
- Pre-push hook allows push when no PR exists for the branch
- Override env var (DSO_ALLOW_PUSH_TO_MERGED_PR=1) bypasses the check
- Test the orchestrator wrapper analogously

## Related

- Direct cause of follow-up PR #168 needing to exist after PR #140 auto-merged
- Cross-references the architectural class of "auto-merge timing" bugs: per-branch-review approves an old commit, OR follow-up commits arrive after merge
data.title: [git pre-push]: Pushing commits to a merged-PR branch silently succeeds -> commits stranded with no merge path
